Series::triu_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::triu_() const -> Series&
Series::triu_(std::int64_t diagonal) const -> Series&

What It Does¶

triu_() is the in-place sibling of triu().

It zeroes the disallowed lower-triangular region directly inside the receiver, then returns that same receiver by reference.

Overload Map¶

triu_()

Equivalent to triu_(0).

triu_(std::int64_t diagonal)

Mutating upper-triangular masking with an explicit keep boundary.

Parameters¶

diagonal (std::int64_t)

The lowest diagonal that remains non-zero after the mutation.

Returns¶

Series& The mutated receiver.

Examples¶

Example 1. triu_() mutates the current Series and returns it.

auto square = pluss::make_series({
    {1, 2, 3},
    {4, 5, 6},
    {7, 8, 9},
}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);

pluss::series::print(std::cout, square.triu_(-1));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=9, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1 2 3 ⎤
⎢ 4 5 6 ⎥
⎣ 0 8 9 ⎦

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • triu_() mutates the receiver. Use triu() when you need a copy.

  • The zero-argument overload is just the main-diagonal case.

  • Because it returns Series&, it can be chained into code that expects the updated object immediately.

Summary¶

Use triu_() when the upper-triangular mask should become the current state of the Series rather than a separate derived result.

See Also¶

  • Series::triu: copy-returning upper-triangular masking.

  • Series::tril_: in-place lower-triangular companion.

  • Series::storage_version: useful when you need to detect later that a mutation occurred.
